model_result.answer_summary: The two [M+Na]+ peaks observed for the hexo-5-enose degradation products of L are at m/z = 455 and m/z = 376. Using integer masses (C=12, H=1, O=16, Na=23): fragment 1 (printed formula C27H28O5) has M = 27*12+28*1+5*16 = 432, so [M+Na]+ = 432+23 = 455; fragment 2 (printed formula C22H25O4) has M = 22*12+25*1+4*16 = 353, so [M+Na]+ = 353+23 = 376.
assumptions: The two degradation-product molecular formulas (C27H28O5 and C22H25O4) are printed verbatim on the Q9-4 problem page/scheme and are taken as problem-given inputs.
Integer (nominal) atomic masses C=12, H=1, O=16, Na=23, as sanctioned by the problem instruction 'Use integer values of atomic mass'.
[M+Na]+ is a singly-charged sodium adduct, so its nominal m/z equals the nominal neutral molecular mass plus the nominal mass of one Na atom (unit charge).
Each drawn product bracket is a closed neutral molecule; the 'O~' squiggle denotes the attachment point to the remainder of L and is properly capped in the isolated product.
